messages.subject: How do diss.dist() and prevosti.dist() "handle" missing data?
messages.subject_clean: How do diss.dist() and prevosti.dist() "handle" missing data?
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am working with a filtered high-density rad-seq ant genomic dataset and am looking into diss.dist() and prevosti.dist() to calculate absolute genetic distance, as an estimate of within-colony pairwise relatedness. I am not interested in population-level relatedness and the genetic population structure of my dataset is quite heterogenous, which is why many other relatedness metrics don't work very well with my dataset.

I am trying to decide whether I should use the missingno() function to remove all loci with missing data from my dataset before calculating genetic distance. The poppr documentation suggests that diss.dist() and prevosti.dist() can "handle" missing data, so this may not be necessary, depending on what is meant by that. For example, if missing data is ignored (i.e. no comparisons between individuals at loci where the data for one of the individuals is missing), that would be ideal. However, if missing data is "handled" by guessing what the most likely allele (i.e. imputation or something like it), this could introduce error into my analysis, particularly because of the aforementioned heterogeneity of my population sample. Does anyone know what exactly the poppr documention means when it says that these functions can "handle" missing data?

Many thanks,

Mari

messages.subject: Writing output to a file
messages.body_plain:
How can I write Euclidean distance for genlight objects to a file?  Morover, why the diversity_stat is shown as NA from
monstat <- diversity_stats(x) > monstat Index Pop H G lambda E.5 [1,] NA NA NA NA

My codes are:
x <- vcfR2genlight(vcf)
library(poppr)
x.dist <- bitwise.dist(x, euclidean = TRUE, scale_missing = TRUE, threads = 1L) ##Works fine
x.dist
monstat <- diversity_stats(x)
monstat

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Writing output to a file
messages.body_plain:
To write a distance matrix to a file, you can convert it to a matrix and use write.table() to write it to disk

write.table(as.matrix(x.dist), file = "dist.csv", sep = ",")

The diversity_stats() function needs a matrix of genotype counts per population as input: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/diversity_stats.html
You supplied the genlight object. You can get the matrix with mlg.table()

All the best,
Zhian.

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Population information
messages.body_plain:
My interpretation of the VCF specification

http://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/

is that there is no 'concept' of population in VCF data. This means that there is no possible way to incorporate population data directly into the VCF data. This is why it needs to be added from some other source, as suggested in the link provided by Zhian.

HTH!
Brian
